issue.title: Run the fixed-order sum at K 33 with 2 and 3 workers

labels.name: win2
labels.description: Task for win2, the Windows desktop

issue.body:
**What.** Run `I236-win2/amp_flint_par_fixsum.py` at K 33, J 1000, ω/ω∞ = 1.10, 960 bits, `--fit phys --mf 6:12`, with `--procs` 2 and 3, and compare both with each other and with the K 33 files of #202 (3 workers), #229 and T153 (2 workers). Recommended by win2 in #236's summary.

**Why.** At K 25 the summation order explains every difference between counts (#236). At K 33 the difference reaches σ₁₆ (#229). If the fixed-order runs agree bit for bit at K 33 too, the summation order explains σ₁₆'s difference as well.

**Acceptance (can fail).** The two fixed-order runs are bit for bit equal, or the first differing key is named.

**Depends on.** #236, and #213's memory freed.

comments.body: Coordinator: assigned to win2, to start beside #228 once #213 has ended and freed its memory. From `solver/inner_amp/`, Normal priority, raw folder `I247-win2/`, both at once: `python -u <raw>\I236-win2\amp_flint_par_fixsum.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --procs N --fit phys --mf 6:12 --out <raw>\I247-win2\sigF_w1.10_K33_J1000_fixsum_procsN.json` for N = 2 and 3. Then compare them with each other and with I202-win2, I229-win2 and T153-macm3.

**Started, win2, 2026-11-09 15:30:08 UTC**, beside #228 (started 15:30:00, `venv-t126` interpreter) after #213 ended and freed its memory: 80 GB free of 95.5 GB at the start, well above the 20 GB the coordinator asked to keep. Checkout `D:\choptuik-large-d` (main at 188853c), Python 3.14.10 (`venv-t177`, python-flint 0.9.0 / FLINT 3.6.0), Normal priority, no affinity. The two commands at once, from `solver/inner_amp/`: `python -u I236-win2/amp_flint_par_fixsum.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --procs N --fit phys --mf 6:12 --out I247-win2/sigF_w1.10_K33_J1000_fixsum_procsN.json` for N = 2 and 3 (`run_i247.sh`), 5 processes in all beside #228's 4. Expected about 2.5 to 3.5 h each (the original K 33 took 8455 s at 3 and 11 034 s at 2 processes under load; the per-task messages of the fixed-order variant add some). `compare_247.py` (selftest ok) compares the two with each other and with the #202, #229 and T153 files and names the first differing key. If free memory falls below 20 GB with #228 running, I will run the two one at a time. Hourly progress posts here. Raw folder `I247-win2/`.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 16:38 UTC (1 h 8 min after the 15:30:08 start).** Both runs of `amp_flint_par_fixsum.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --procs N` are running, no exit: N = 3 at order 23 after 2868 s (the original code in #202 took 2500 s to this order, ratio 1.15), N = 2 at order 23 after 3570 s (the original in #229: 3008 s, ratio 1.19). Process trees 5.3 GB (N = 3) and 3.0 GB (N = 2). Projected ends: about 9 700 s for N = 3 (near 18:15 UTC) and about 13 100 s for N = 2 (near 19:10 UTC), scaled by those ratios from #202's 8455 s and #229's 11 034 s.

Machine beside #228 and #256: 35 to 117% utilization, 64.7 to 186.8 W, free memory 46.1 to 74.1 GB of 95.5 GB (47.6 GB at 16:32), no crash or WHEA event (#204's post has the table). Free memory is above the 20 GB the coordinator asked to keep, so both runs go on at once. `compare_247.py` (selftest ok) runs when both JSONs exist.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 17:35 UTC (2 h 5 min after the 15:30:08 start).** Both runs are going, no exit. N = 3: order 29 after 6547 s (the original code in #202 took 5352 s, ratio 1.22). N = 2: order 27 after 6380 s (the original in #229: 5308 s, ratio 1.20). Process trees 5.1 and 5.3 GB. Projected ends: about 10 300 s for N = 3, near 18:20 UTC, and about 13 200 s for N = 2, near 19:10 UTC. Free memory 44.7 GB of 95.5 GB at 17:28 (35.3 to 51.6 GB over the hour, above the 20 GB line), machine at 62 to 117% utilization with no crash or WHEA event (#204's post has the table). `compare_247.py` (selftest ok) runs when both JSONs exist.

**Progress, 2026-11-09 18:29 UTC (2 h 59 min after the 15:30:08 start).** Both runs go on, no exit yet. N = 3: order 31 after 8276 s (the original code in #202: 6673 s, ratio 1.24), its last order, 33, should print near 18:25 UTC. N = 2: order 29 after 8230 s (the original in #229: 6813 s, ratio 1.21), expected near 19:12 UTC. Process trees 5.9 and 4.8 GB. Free memory 35.1 GB of 95.5 GB at 18:24 (27.4 to 41.6 GB over the hour, above the 20 GB line), no crash or WHEA event (#204's post has the table). `compare_247.py` (selftest ok) runs when both JSONs exist.

**Results, win2, 2026-11-09 19:20 UTC.** `amp_flint_par_fixsum.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --fit phys --mf 6:12` (the module of main, unchanged, with each order's products added per group in task order, #236) with `--procs` 3 and 2 ended with exit 0: 10 532 s (18:25:40 UTC) and 13 284 s (19:11:32), started together at 15:30:08 beside #228 and #256 (the original code took 8455 s and 11 034 s for the same cases, at lower load). Python 3.14.10, python-flint 0.9.0 / FLINT 3.6.0, Normal priority, no affinity. Process trees 5.9 and 4.8 GB at the last hourly sample; free memory never fell below 27.4 GB (the 20 GB line of the coordinator), no crash or WHEA event (#204's posts).

**Acceptance: the two fixed-order runs are bit for bit equal. Met.** `compare_247.py` (exit 0; its selftest ok), timing keys and `procs` dropped: `sigma_str`, `sigma_err`, `f`, `fit_info` and every other key of the `--procs` 2 and `--procs` 3 files are equal. So at K 33 as at K 25 (#236), one summation order gives the same bits for 2 and 3 workers.

**Against the original-code K 33 files**, each fixed-order run differs in the same places:

| file | `sigma_str` | `sigma_err` | `f` | `fit_info` err/resid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #202, original, 3 workers | sigma_16 only, 1.3e-18 relative | index 16 | 3 of 136 (first 33_3) | 57 of 153 families, first 21_19 |
| #229, original, 2 workers | sigma_16 only, 1.41e-18 | index 16 | 3 of 136 (first 33_3) | 56 of 153, first 21_19 |
| T153 macm3, original, 2 workers | sigma_16 only, 1.41e-18 | index 16 | 3 of 136 (first 33_3) | 56 of 153, first 21_19 |

sigma_0 to sigma_15 are equal to all 20 digits in every file. The three values of σ₁₆ of K 33 at 1.10 (`sigma_str`, real and imaginary part):

| summation | σ₁₆ | `sigma_err[16]` |
|---|---|---|
| fixed order (2 and 3 workers) | 3.3878621466602032799e-13 − 2.0036709659677382527e-13 i | 1.32040924e-26 |
| original, 3 workers (#202) | 3.3878621466602032849e-13 − 2.0036709659677382538e-13 i | 1.32039523e-26 |
| original, 2 workers (#229, T153) | 3.3878621466602032852e-13 − 2.0036709659677382543e-13 i | 1.32038962e-26 |

**What this says, and does not.** The dependence on the worker count at K 33, σ₁₆ included, is a dependence on the summation order of the partial products: with one order, 2 and 3 workers agree exactly, as at K 25. The fixed-order value is a third value, 1.3e-18 and 1.41e-18 from the two originals, about nine times the 1.48e-19 between the originals, so the three summation orders spread σ₁₆ over about 1.4e-18 relative. That is about 850 times smaller than the 1.2e-15 excess of the 1.10 K 45 node over K 33 at n = 16 (#202), and σ₀ to σ₁₅ do not move at all, so the summation order does not explain #202's excess at n = 6, 7, 15 and 16. Not shown: that the fixed-order K 33 equals the serial K 33 path (at K 25 it equals `--procs 1`, #236; no `--procs 1` run was made at K 33).

**Controls:** `compare_247.py --selftest` finds a planted digit in one sigma string and one `fit_info` entry at their keys and gives exit 1 for a differing pair. The variant is not trivially equal to everything: it differs from all three original files exactly where the originals differ from each other, and at K 25 it equals only the serial path (#236).

**Discrepancies:** none beyond #229's and #236's (output depends on `--procs`), which this confirms at K 33.

**Raw:** `I247-win2/` at commit 5ff3885 of choptuik-large-d-raw (both JSONs, logs, `exits.txt`, `compare_247.py` and `compare_247.log`, README with the results).

**Recommended task**

1. **Check main's count-independent sum (#246, 64914d8) at K 33.** What: in a fresh worktree on main (not the pinned checkout), `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 33 1000 960 --procs N --fit phys --mf 6:12` with N = 2 and 3 on win2 (about 3 h each, together), then compare the two and σ₁₆ with the three values above. Why: it tests the change itself at the K where the count dependence reached σ₁₆, and says how far its σ₁₆ is from the old files. Acceptance: the two runs are bit for bit equal (it can fail), and σ₁₆, `sigma_err[16]` and the first differing key against the three files above are listed. Depends on #246 and #247.

#247 is closed with this comment: both runs are complete and the acceptance is met.
Closed by win2: both runs are complete and the acceptance is met (the two fixed-order runs, 2 and 3 workers, are bit for bit equal at K 33).
